S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days of learning of it, and notify affected customers within 10 business days when the incident may indicate a safety risk. Imminent hazards must be reported to regulators and affected customers without delay, and no later than 24 hours after discovery.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and at least every 3 years thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Before purchase, purchasers must receive the full test results, including the failure rate, for the model they are considering. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator notification, a corrective-action plan, and retesting on a regulator-approved schedule; it does not by itself prohibit continued production.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market 2 years after this standard takes effect must support secure remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must provide a practical retrofit for installed units that can support the function, completing the retrofit within 6 years after the effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units placed on the market 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved safety and reliability protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model’s verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and provide incident and corrective-action data. Regulators shall assess the evidence, including incident severity, test results, and corrective actions, and may require a recall or other protective action where warranted.

document.section_notes: The final rules weaken S1 (serious incidents reported in 5 business days rather than 48h), S2 (5% failure rate triggers corrective action but no sales ban), S3 (new units get 24 months and retrofit is 6 years with a feasibility condition), and S5 (8/100k trigger only requires regulator notification, not mandatory recall). S4 is acceptable with built-in suppression required at 36 months. Both red lines are satisfied: per-model results go to purchasers but not the public, and the 36-month suppression deadline matches Halcyon's red line.
